text: For pulsating DC voltages (alternating voltages without change of polarity) the DC threshold shall be applied when assessing the specific voltage condition.
condition: for pulsating DC voltages

text: The "H" point for each seat shall be determined in accordance with the procedure described in Annex 6.
When the protective system for the front seating positions includes belts, the belt components shall meet the requirements of Regulation No. 16.
condition: when the protective system for the front seating positions includes belts

text: Seating positions where a dummy is installed and the protective system includes belts shall be provided with anchorage points conforming to Regulation No. 14.
condition: seating positions where a dummy is installed and the protective system includes belts

text: The vehicle shall be tested and approved in accordance with the method described in Annex 3 (Full Width Rigid Barrier test).

The vehicle which, in agreement with the Technical Service, is considered as having the worst case effect on the result of the injury criteria specified in paragraph 5.2.1. shall be selected for the restraint system test.
The test carried out in accordance with Annex 3 shall be considered satisfactory only if all the conditions set out in paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.7. are all satisfied at the same time.
Vehicles equipped with electric power train shall additionally meet the requirements of paragraph 5.2.8.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: The requirements of paragraph 5.2.8. may be met by a separate impact test at the request of the manufacturer and after validation by the Technical Service, provided that the electrical components do not influence the occupant protection performance of the vehicle type as defined in paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.5.; in that case the requirements of paragraph 5.2.8. shall be checked in accordance with the methods of Annex 3, except paragraphs 2., 5. and 6. of Annex 3.
condition: if a separate impact test for electrical safety is requested by the manufacturer

text: A dummy corresponding to the specifications for Hybrid III fiftieth percentile, fitted with a 45° ankle angle and meeting the specifications for its adjustment, shall be installed in the driver's seat.

A dummy corresponding to the specifications for Hybrid III fifth percentile, fitted with a 45° ankle angle and meeting the specifications for its adjustment, shall be installed in the outboard passenger's seat.
The performance criteria described in Annex 4 shall be recorded in accordance with Annex 8 on the dummies in the front outboard seats and shall meet the conditions of paragraphs 5.2.1.1. and 5.2.1.2.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the head performance criterion (HPC) shall not exceed 1000.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the resultant head acceleration shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively, excluding rebound movement of the head.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the axial tensile neck force shall not exceed 3.3 kN.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface shall not exceed 3.1 kN.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the neck bending moment about the y axis shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) shall not exceed 42 mm.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the viscous criterion (V * C) for the thorax shall not exceed 1.0 m/s.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile adult male dummy, the femur force criterion (FFC) shall not exceed 9.07 kN.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the head performance criterion (HPC) shall not exceed 1000.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the resultant head acceleration shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively, excluding rebound movement of the head.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the axial tensile neck force shall not exceed 2.9 kN.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface shall not exceed 2.7 kN.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the neck bending moment about the y axis shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) shall not exceed 34 mm in the case of vehicles of category M1.

For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) shall not exceed 34 mm in the case of vehicles of category N1 with a maximum permissible mass not exceeding 2,800 kg, a maximum vehicle width not exceeding 1,480 mm and a length not exceeding 3,400 mm.
condition: maximum permissible mass not exceeding 2,800 kg, maximum vehicle width not exceeding 1,480 mm and length not exceeding 3,400 mm

text: For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) shall not exceed 42 mm in the case of vehicles of category N1 with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 2,800 kg, or with a maximum vehicle width exceeding 1,480 mm or with a length exceeding 3,400 mm.
condition: maximum permissible mass exceeding 2,800 kg, or maximum vehicle width exceeding 1,480 mm, or length exceeding 3,400 mm

text: For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the viscous criterion (V * C) for the thorax shall not exceed 1.0 m/s.
For the Hybrid III fifth percentile adult female dummy, the femur force criterion (FFC) shall not exceed 7 kN.
After the test the residual steering wheel displacement, measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub, shall not exceed 80 mm in the upwards vertical direction.
After the test the residual steering wheel displacement, measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub, shall not exceed 100 mm in the rearward horizontal direction.
Vehicles meeting the steering wheel displacement requirements of either Regulations Nos. 12 or 94 are deemed to comply with the steering wheel displacement requirement of paragraph 5.2.2.1.
condition: if the vehicle meets the steering wheel displacement requirements of Regulation No. 12 or No. 94

text: During the test no door shall open.

In the case of automatically activated door locking systems which are installed optionally and/or which can be de-activated by the driver, the requirement that no door opens during the test shall be verified by using one of the two test procedures of paragraphs 5.2.3.1.1. or 5.2.3.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
condition: automatically activated door locking system installed optionally and/or de-activatable by the driver

text: If testing in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1., the manufacturer shall in addition demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Technical Service (e.g. manufacturer's in-house data) that, in the absence of the system or when the system is de-activated, no door will open in case of the impact.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatically activated door locking system tested per Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1.

text: Alternatively, the door opening verification test is conducted in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.2.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatically activated door locking system, at the choice of the manufacturer

text: After the impact, the side doors shall be unlocked.
In the case of vehicles equipped with an automatically activated door locking system, the doors shall be locked before the moment of impact.
condition: vehicles equipped with an automatically activated door locking system

text: In the case of vehicles equipped with an automatically activated door locking system, the doors shall be unlocked after the impact.
condition: vehicles equipped with an automatically activated door locking system

text: In the case of vehicles equipped with automatically activated door locking systems which are installed optionally and/or which can be de-activated by the driver, the side door unlocking requirement shall be verified by using one of the two test procedures of paragraphs 5.2.4.2.1. or 5.2.4.2.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
condition: automatically activated door locking system installed optionally and/or de-activatable by the driver

text: If testing in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1., the manufacturer shall in addition demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Technical Service (e.g. manufacturer's in-house data) that, in the absence of the system or when the system is de-activated, no locking of the side doors shall occur during the impact.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatically activated door locking system tested per Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.1.

text: Alternatively, the side door unlocking verification test is conducted in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 1.4.3.5.2.2.
condition: optional/de-activatable automatically activated door locking system, at the choice of the manufacturer

text: After the impact, it shall be possible, without the use of tools except for those necessary to support the weight of the dummy, to open at least one door per row of seats.
condition: not applicable to convertibles where the top can be easily opened to allow the evacuation of the occupants

text: Where there is no door per row of seats, it shall be possible after the impact, without the use of tools except for those necessary to support the weight of the dummy, to allow the evacuation of all the occupants by activating the displacement system of seats, if necessary.
condition: where there is no door for a row of seats; not applicable to convertibles where the top can be easily opened

text: The post-impact door opening/evacuation capability shall be assessed for all configurations or the worst-case configuration for the number of doors on each side of the vehicle and for both left-hand drive and right-hand drive vehicles, when applicable.

After the impact, it shall be possible, without the use of tools except for those necessary to support the weight of the dummy, to release the dummies from their restraint system, which, locked, shall be capable of being released by a maximum force of 60 N on the centre of the release control.
After the impact, it shall be possible, without the use of tools except for those necessary to support the weight of the dummy, to remove the dummies from the vehicle without adjustment of the seats.
In the case of a vehicle propelled by liquid fuel, no more than slight leakage of liquid from the fuel feed installation shall occur on collision.
condition: vehicle propelled by liquid fuel

text: If there is continuous leakage of liquid from the fuel-feed installation after the collision, the rate of leakage shall not exceed 30 g/min.
condition: vehicle propelled by liquid fuel with continuous leakage after the collision

text: If the liquid from the fuel-feed system mixes with liquids from the other systems and the various liquids cannot easily be separated and identified, all the liquids collected shall be taken into account in evaluating the continuous leakage.
condition: if fuel mixes with other liquids that cannot easily be separated and identified

text: In the case of a compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle, compliance with paragraphs 5.2.7.1. to 5.2.7.3. shall be shown.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The hydrogen leakage rate (VH2), determined in accordance with paragraph 4. of Annex 10 for hydrogen or paragraph 5. of Annex 10 for helium, shall not exceed an average of 118 NL per minute for the time interval, Δt minutes, after the crash.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The hydrogen concentration by volume in air determined for the passenger and luggage compartments in accordance with paragraph 6. of Annex 10 shall not exceed 4.0 per cent at any time throughout the 60 minute post-crash measurement period.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle tested with hydrogen

text: The helium concentration by volume in air determined for the passenger and luggage compartments in accordance with paragraph 6. of Annex 10 shall not exceed 3.0 per cent at any time throughout the 60 minute post-crash measurement period.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle tested with helium

text: The gas concentration requirement is satisfied if it is confirmed that the shut-off valve of each compressed hydrogen storage system has closed within five seconds of first vehicle contact with the barrier and there is no leakage from the compressed hydrogen storage system(s).
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle, as alternative demonstration

text: The container(s) for hydrogen storage shall remain attached to the vehicle at a minimum of one attachment point.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Following the test conducted in accordance with Annex 3, the electric power train operating on high voltage and the high voltage systems galvanically connected to the high voltage bus of the electric power train shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2.8.1. to 5.2.8.4.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train operating on high voltage

text: After the impact, the high voltage buses shall meet at least one of the four criteria specified in paragraphs 5.2.8.1.1. through 5.2.8.1.4.2. (absence of high voltage, low electrical energy, physical protection, isolation resistance).
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: If the vehicle has an automatic disconnect function, or device(s) that conductively divide the electric power train circuit during driving condition, at least one of the electrical shock protection criteria shall apply to the disconnected circuit or to each divided circuit individually after the disconnect function is activated.
condition: vehicle with automatic disconnect function or devices dividing the electric power train circuit

text: The isolation resistance criteria of paragraph 5.2.8.1.4. shall not apply if more than a single potential of a part of the high voltage bus is not protected under the conditions of protection degree IPXXB.
condition: if more than a single potential of a part of the high voltage bus is not protected to IPXXB

text: If the crash test is performed with part(s) of the high voltage system not energized, the protection against electrical shock shall be proved by either physical protection (paragraph 5.2.8.1.3.) or isolation resistance (paragraph 5.2.8.1.4.) for the relevant part(s), with the exception of any coupling system for charging the REESS which is not energized during driving condition.
condition: crash test performed with part(s) of the high voltage system not energized
applies_to: coupling system for charging the rees

text: Absence of high voltage: the voltages Ub, U1 and U2 of the high voltage buses shall be equal or less than 30 VAC or 60 VDC within 60 seconds after the impact when measured in accordance with paragraph 2. of Annex 9.
condition: if the absence of high voltage criterion is used

text: Low electrical energy: the Total Energy (TE) on the high voltage buses shall be less than 0.2 joules when measured according to paragraph 3. of Annex 9 with formula (a), or alternatively calculated from the measured voltage Ub and the manufacturer-specified X-capacitor capacitance (Cx) according to formula (b).
condition: if the low electrical energy criterion is used

text: The energy stored in the Y-capacitors (TEy1, TEy2) shall also be less than 0.2 joules, calculated by measuring the voltages U1 and U2 between the high voltage buses and the electrical chassis and the manufacturer-specified Y-capacitor capacitance according to formula (c) of paragraph 3. of Annex 9.
condition: if the low electrical energy criterion is used

text: Physical protection: for protection against direct contact with high voltage live parts, the protection degree IPXXB shall be provided, assessed in accordance with paragraph 4 of Annex 9.
condition: if the physical protection criterion is used

text: For protection against indirect contact, the resistance between all exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures and the electrical chassis shall be lower than 0.1 Ω when there is current flow of at least 0.2 A.
condition: if the physical protection criterion is used

text: The resistance between any two simultaneously reachable exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures that are less than 2.5 m from each other shall be less than 0.2 Ω when there is current flow of at least 0.2 A.
condition: if the physical protection criterion is used

text: The indirect contact resistance requirements are satisfied if the galvanic connection has been made by welding; in case of doubt or if the connection is established by means other than welding, measurements shall be made using one of the test procedures of paragraph 4.1. of Annex 9 (resistance may be calculated from separately measured resistances of the relevant parts of the electric path).
condition: if the physical protection criterion is used

text: Isolation resistance: the criteria of paragraphs 5.2.8.1.4.1. and 5.2.8.1.4.2. shall be met, with the measurement conducted in accordance with paragraph 5. of Annex 9.
condition: if the isolation resistance criterion is used

text: If the AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, the isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis (Ri) shall have a minimum value of 100 Ω/V of the working voltage for DC buses.
condition: separate galvanically isolated DC and AC buses; isolation resistance criterion used

text: If the AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, the isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis (Ri) shall have a minimum value of 500 Ω/V of the working voltage for AC buses.
condition: separate galvanically isolated DC and AC buses; isolation resistance criterion used

text: If the AC and DC high voltage buses are conductively connected, they shall meet one of the requirements (a), (b) or (c) of paragraph 5.2.8.1.4.2.
condition: combined conductively connected DC and AC buses; isolation resistance criterion used

text: Option (a): isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 500 Ω/V of the working voltage.
condition: combined conductively connected DC and AC buses, if option (a) is chosen

text: Option (b): isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 100 Ω/V of the working voltage and the AC bus shall meet the physical protection described in paragraph 5.2.8.1.3.
condition: combined conductively connected DC and AC buses, if option (b) is chosen

text: Option (c): isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 100 Ω/V of the working voltage and the AC bus shall meet the absence of high voltage described in paragraph 5.2.8.1.1.
condition: combined conductively connected DC and AC buses, if option (c) is chosen

text: For aqueous electrolyte REESS, for a period from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact, there shall be no electrolyte leakage from the REESS into the passenger compartment.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: For aqueous electrolyte REESS, for a period from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact, no more than 7 per cent by volume of the REESS electrolyte, with a maximum of 5.0 l, shall leak from the REESS to the outside of the passenger compartment.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: For containers containing Stoddard, coloured coolant and electrolyte, the fluids shall be allowed to separate by specific gravity and then be measured.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS, collected fluids mixed

text: For non-aqueous electrolyte REESS, for a period from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact, there shall be no liquid electrolyte leakage from the REESS into the passenger compartment or luggage compartment and no liquid electrolyte leakage to outside the vehicle.
condition: non-aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: The non-aqueous electrolyte leakage requirement shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the vehicle.
condition: non-aqueous electrolyte REESS

text: After the impact, the REESS shall remain attached to the vehicle by at least one component anchorage, bracket, or any structure that transfers loads from REESS to the vehicle structure.
condition: vehicles equipped with REESS

text: A REESS located outside the passenger compartment shall not enter the passenger compartment during the impact test.
condition: REESS located outside the passenger compartment

text: For a period from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact, there shall be no evidence of fire or explosion from the REESS.
condition: vehicles equipped with REESS

text: For a vehicle fitted with airbag assemblies intended to protect the driver and occupants other than the driver, compliance with paragraphs 8.1.8. to 8.1.9. of UN Regulation No. 16 as amended by the 08 series of amendments (instructions for users) shall be demonstrated as from 1 September 2020 for new vehicle types; before this date the relevant requirements of the preceding series of amendments apply.
condition: vehicle fitted with airbag assemblies for the driver and occupants other than the driver

text: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
Every vehicle approved under this Regulation shall be manufactured so as to conform to the vehicle type approved and satisfy the requirements set forth in paragraphs 5. and 6.
The Type Approval Authority which has granted type approval may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility.
The normal frequency of verifications of the conformity control methods shall be once every two years.
The approval mark dimension a shall be at least 8 mm, as shown in the arrangements of approval marks (Models A and B).
The test area shall be large enough to accommodate the run-up track, barrier and technical installations necessary for the test.
The last part of the track, for at least 5 m before the barrier, shall be horizontal, flat and smooth.
The barrier shall consist of a block of reinforced concrete not less than 3 m wide in front and not less than 1.5 m high.
The barrier shall be of such thickness that it weighs at least 70 metric tons.
The front face of the barrier shall be flat, vertical and perpendicular to the axis of the run-up track.
The front face of the barrier shall be covered with plywood boards 20 ± 2 mm thick, in good condition.
A structure on a steel plate at least 25 mm thick may be placed between the plywood board and the barrier.
condition: if such a structure is used

text: A barrier with different characteristics may be used only provided that the area of the impact surface is greater than the frontal crash area of the vehicle being tested and that it gives equivalent results.
condition: if a barrier with different characteristics is used

text: The vehicle shall reach the obstacle on a course perpendicular to the collision wall, with a maximum lateral misalignment of ± 30 cm between the vertical median line of the front of the vehicle and the vertical median line of the collision wall.
The test vehicle shall be representative of the series production, shall include all the equipment normally fitted and shall be in normal running order.
Components of the test vehicle may be replaced by equivalent masses only where this substitution clearly has no noticeable effect on the results measured under paragraph 6.
condition: if components are replaced by equivalent masses

text: The fuel system may be modified, by agreement between manufacturer and Technical Service, so that an appropriate amount of fuel can be used to run the engine or the electrical energy conversion system.
condition: by agreement between manufacturer and Technical Service

text: For the test, the mass of the vehicle submitted shall be the unladen kerb mass.
The fuel tank shall be filled with water to mass equal to 90 per cent of the mass of a full load of fuel as specified by the manufacturer with a tolerance of ±1 per cent.
condition: not applicable to hydrogen fuel tanks

text: If the other systems (brake, cooling ...) are empty, the mass of the liquids shall be compensated.
condition: if other systems are emptied

text: If the mass of the measuring apparatus on board the vehicle exceeds the 25 kg allowed, it may be compensated by reductions which have no noticeable effect on the results measured under paragraph 6.
condition: if the measuring apparatus mass exceeds 25 kg

text: The mass of the measuring apparatus shall not change each axle reference load by more than 5 per cent, each variation not exceeding 20 kg.
The mass of the vehicle resulting from paragraph 1.4.2.1 shall be indicated in the report.

The steering wheel, if adjustable, shall be placed in the normal position indicated by the manufacturer or, in the absence of any particular recommendation by the manufacturer, midway between the limits of its range(s) of adjustment.
condition: if the steering wheel is adjustable

text: At the end of the propelled travel, the steering wheel shall be left free, with its spokes in the position which according to the manufacturer corresponds to straight-ahead travel of the vehicle.

The movable glazing of the vehicle shall be in the closed position; for test measurement purposes and in agreement with the manufacturer it may be lowered, provided that the position of the operating handle corresponds to the closed position.
The gear-change lever shall be in the neutral position.
condition: unless the vehicle is propelled by its own engine

text: If the vehicle is propelled by its own engine, the gear-change lever position shall be defined by the manufacturer.
condition: if the vehicle is propelled by its own engine

text: The pedals shall be in their normal position of rest.
Adjustable pedals shall be set in their mid-position unless another position is specified by the manufacturer.
condition: if the pedals are adjustable

text: The doors shall be closed but not locked.

The automatically activated door locking system shall be activated at the start of propulsion of the vehicle in order to lock the doors automatically before the moment of impact, or at the choice of the manufacturer the doors shall be locked manually before the start of propulsion.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with an automatically activated door locking system

text: One of the two procedures of paragraphs 1.4.3.5.2.1 or 1.4.3.5.2.2 shall be used, at the choice of the manufacturer.
condition: if the automatically activated door locking system is installed optionally and/or can be de-activated by the driver

text: The automatically activated door locking system shall be activated at the start of propulsion of the vehicle in order to lock the doors automatically before the moment of impact, or at the choice of the manufacturer the doors shall be locked manually before the start of propulsion.
condition: if the system is optional and/or can be de-activated and this procedure is chosen

text: The side doors on the driver side shall be unlocked and the automatically activated door locking system overridden for these doors.
condition: if the system is optional and/or can be de-activated and this procedure is chosen

text: For the side doors on the passenger side, the system may be activated to lock these doors automatically before the moment of impact, or at the choice of the manufacturer these doors shall be locked manually before the start of propulsion; the test is deemed fulfilled if the unlocked and locked doors are reversed.
condition: if the system is optional and/or can be de-activated and this procedure is chosen

text: If an opening or removable roof is fitted, it shall be in place and in the closed position; for test measurement purposes and in agreement with the manufacturer it may be open.
condition: if an opening or removable roof is fitted

text: The sun-visors shall be in the stowed position.
The interior rear-view mirror shall be in the normal position of use.
Arm-rests at the front and rear, if movable, shall be in the lowered position, unless this is prevented by the position of the dummies in the vehicle.
condition: if arm-rests are movable

text: Head restraints adjustable for height shall be in their appropriate position as defined by the manufacturer.
condition: if head restraints are adjustable for height

text: In the absence of any manufacturer recommendation, head restraints shall be in their uppermost position for the 50th percentile male dummy and in the lowermost position for the 5th percentile female dummy.
condition: if adjustable for height and no manufacturer recommendation

text: Longitudinally adjustable front driver seats shall be placed so that their "H" point, determined per Annex 6, is in the middle position of travel or in the nearest locking position thereto, and at the height position defined by the manufacturer (if independently adjustable for height); for a bench seat, the reference shall be the "H" point of the driver's place.
condition: if the driver seat is adjustable longitudinally

text: Longitudinally adjustable front passenger seats shall be placed so that their "H" point, determined per Annex 6, is in the position given by the manufacturer, which shall be forward of the middle position of travel.
condition: if the passenger seat is adjustable longitudinally and a manufacturer position is given

text: In the absence of a manufacturer recommendation, the front passenger seat "H" point shall be as near as possible to a position midway between the forward most position of the seat and the centre position of its travel.
condition: if adjustable longitudinally and no manufacturer recommendation

text: Any support system of the front passenger seat shall be adjusted as defined by the manufacturer, or in the absence of recommendation (e.g. seat cushion length and tilt adjustment) shall be in its retracted/lowermost position.

Adjustable front seat-backs shall be adjusted so that the resulting torso inclination of the dummy is as close as possible to that recommended by the manufacturer for normal use or, in the absence of recommendation, to 25° towards the rear from the vertical.
condition: if seat-backs are adjustable

text: For the 5th percentile female dummy, the seat back may be adjusted to a different angle only if needed to respect the requirements of Annex 5, paragraph 3.1.2.
condition: for the 5th percentile female dummy seat

text: If adjustable, the rear seats or rear bench seats shall be placed in the rearmost position.
condition: if rear seats are adjustable

text: The adjustment of SOC shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C.
condition: vehicles with electric power train

text: Where different charging procedures are possible, the REESS shall be charged using the procedure which yields the highest SOC.
condition: where different charging procedures are possible

text: For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be externally charged, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC in accordance with the procedure specified by the manufacturer for normal operation until the charging process is normally terminated.
condition: REESS designed to be externally charged

text: For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC achievable with normal operation of the vehicle, and the manufacturer shall advise on the vehicle operation mode to achieve this SOC.
condition: REESS charged only by an on-vehicle energy source

text: When the vehicle is tested, the SOC shall be no less than 95 per cent of the SOC according to paragraphs 1.4.4.1.1 and 1.4.4.1.2 for REESS designed to be externally charged.
condition: REESS designed to be externally charged

text: When the vehicle is tested, the SOC shall be no less than 90 per cent of the SOC according to paragraphs 1.4.4.1.1 and 1.4.4.1.2 for REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle; the SOC is confirmed by a method provided by the manufacturer.
condition: REESS charged only by an on-vehicle energy source

text: The electric power train shall be energized with or without the operation of the original electrical energy sources (e.g. engine-generator, REESS or electric energy conversion system).
condition: vehicles with electric power train

text: By agreement between Technical Service and manufacturer, the test may be performed with all or parts of the electric power train not energized insofar as there is no negative influence on the test result; for non-energized parts, protection against electrical shock shall be proved by either physical protection or isolation resistance and appropriate additional evidence.
condition: if parts of the electric power train are not energized

text: Where an automatic disconnect is provided, the test may be performed at the manufacturer's request with the automatic disconnect triggered; in this case it shall be demonstrated that the automatic disconnect would have operated during the impact test, including the automatic activation signal and the galvanic separation under the conditions seen during the impact.
condition: if an automatic disconnect is provided and the test is performed with it triggered

text: A Hybrid III fiftieth percentile male dummy meeting the specifications for its adjustment shall be installed in the driver seat in accordance with Annex 5.
A Hybrid III fifth percentile female dummy meeting the specifications for its adjustment shall be installed in the passenger seat in accordance with Annex 5.
The car shall be tested with restraint systems as provided by the manufacturer.
The vehicle shall be propelled by its own engine or by any other propelling device.
At the moment of impact the vehicle shall no longer be subject to the action of any additional steering or propelling device.
The course of the vehicle shall be such that it satisfies the requirements of paragraphs 1.2 and 1.3.1 of Annex 3.
Vehicle speed at the moment of impact shall be 50 -0/+1 km/h; a test performed at a higher impact speed in which the vehicle met the requirements shall be considered satisfactory.
All measurements necessary for the verification of the performance criteria shall be made with measurement systems corresponding to the specifications of Annex 8.
The different dummy parameters shall be recorded through independent data channels of the specified CFC.
The dummy head acceleration referring to the centre of gravity shall be calculated from the triaxial components of the acceleration measured with a CFC of 1000.
The axial tensile force and the fore/aft shear force at the dummy neck/head interface shall be measured with a CFC of 1000.
The bending moment about a lateral axis at the dummy neck/head interface shall be measured with a CFC of 600.
The dummy chest deflection between the sternum and the spine shall be measured with a CFC of 180.
The dummy femur axial compressive force shall be measured with a CFC of 600.

The deceleration time history of the structure shall be determined from the longitudinal accelerometers at the base of one of the "B" pillars of the vehicle with a CFC of 180 by means of data channels meeting Annex 8.
The speed time history used in the Annex 7 test procedure shall be obtained from the longitudinal accelerometer at the "B" pillar.
Alternative test procedures may be permitted at the discretion of the Type Approval Authority only provided equivalence can be demonstrated.
condition: if an alternative procedure is used

text: A report shall be attached to the approval documentation describing the method used and the results obtained or the reason for not carrying out the test.
condition: if an alternative procedure is used

text: Responsibility for demonstrating the equivalence of the alternative method shall rest with the manufacturer or his agent wishing to use such a method.
condition: if an alternative procedure is used

text: The Head Performance Criterion (HPC36) is considered satisfied when, during the test, there is no contact between the head and any vehicle component.

If there is contact between the head and any vehicle component during the test, HPC shall be calculated on the basis of the resultant acceleration measured according to paragraph 5.2.1 of Annex 3, expressed in g (1 g = 9,81 m/s2).
condition: if head contact occurs

text: If the beginning of head contact can be determined satisfactorily, t1 and t2 shall define an interval between the beginning of head contact and the end of the recording for which HPC is maximum.
condition: if the beginning of head contact can be determined

text: If the beginning of head contact cannot be determined, t1 and t2 shall define a time interval between the beginning and the end of the recording for which HPC is maximum.
condition: if the beginning of head contact cannot be determined

text: Values of HPC for which the time interval (t1 - t2) is greater than 36 ms shall be ignored for the purposes of calculating the maximum value.

The resultant head acceleration during forward impact which is exceeded for 3 ms cumulatively shall be calculated from the resultant head acceleration measured according to paragraph 5.2.1 of Annex 3.
The neck injury criteria shall be determined by the axial tensile force and the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface, expressed in kN and measured according to paragraph 5.2.2 of Annex 3.
The neck bending moment criterion shall be determined by the bending moment, expressed in Nm, about a lateral axis at the head/neck interface, measured according to paragraph 5.2.2 of Annex 3.
The thorax compression criterion shall be determined by the absolute value of the thorax deformation, expressed in mm and measured according to paragraph 5.2.3 of Annex 3.
The viscous criterion (V * C) shall be calculated as the instantaneous product of the compression and the rate of deflection of the sternum, measured according to paragraph 5.2.3 of Annex 3.
The femur force criterion shall be determined by the compression load expressed in kN, transmitted axially on each femur of the dummy and measured according to paragraph 5.2.4 of Annex 3.
The viscous criterion shall be calculated as the instantaneous product of the compression and the rate of deflection of the sternum, both derived from the measurement of sternum deflection.

The sternum deflection response shall be filtered once at CFC 180 and the compression at time t calculated as C(t) = D(t) / constant, with constant = 0.229 for the HIII 50th and constant = 0.187 for the HIII 5th.
The maximum value of the time interval ∂t between deflection measurements used for calculating sternum deflection velocity shall be 1.25 x 10-4 seconds.
For separate seats, the plane of symmetry of the dummy shall coincide with the vertical median plane of the seat.
condition: separate seats

text: On a front bench seat, the plane of symmetry of the driver dummy shall lie in the vertical plane passing through the steering wheel centre and parallel to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
condition: front bench seat

text: If the driver seating position of a front bench seat is determined by the shape of the bench, such seat shall be regarded as a separate seat.
condition: seating position determined by the shape of the bench

text: On a front bench seat, the plane of symmetry of the outer passenger dummy shall be symmetrical with that of the driver dummy relative to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
condition: front bench seat

text: If the outer passenger seating position of a front bench seat is determined by the shape of the bench, such seat shall be regarded as a separate seat.
condition: seating position determined by the shape of the bench

text: On a bench seat for front passengers (not including driver), the planes of symmetry of the dummy shall coincide with the median planes of the seating positions defined by the manufacturer.
condition: bench seat for front passengers not including driver

text: The transverse instrumentation platform of the head of the HIII fiftieth percentile driver dummy shall be horizontal within 2.5°.

To level the head of the HIII fiftieth percentile driver dummy in vehicles with upright seats with non-adjustable backs, first the H point position shall be adjusted within the limits of paragraph 2.4.3.1, then if still not level the pelvic angle within the limits of paragraph 2.4.3.2, then if still not level the neck bracket the minimum amount necessary to make the head instrumentation platform horizontal within 2.5°.
condition: upright seats with non-adjustable backs

text: The driver dummy's upper arms shall be adjacent to the torso with the centrelines as close to a vertical plane as possible.
The palms of the driver test dummy shall be in contact with the outer part of the steering wheel rim at the rim's horizontal centreline.

The thumbs of the driver test dummy shall be over the steering wheel rim and lightly taped to it so that if the hand is pushed upward by a force of not less than 9 N and not more than 22 N, the tape releases the hand from the steering wheel rim.
In vehicles equipped with bench seats, the upper torso of the driver test dummy shall rest against the seat back.
condition: vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: In vehicles equipped with bench seats, the midsagittal plane of the driver dummy shall be vertical and parallel to the vehicle's longitudinal centreline, and pass through the centre of the steering wheel rim.
condition: vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: In vehicles equipped with individual seats, the upper torso of the driver test dummy shall rest against the seat back.
condition: vehicles equipped with individual seats

text: In vehicles equipped with individual seats, the midsagittal plane of the driver dummy shall be vertical and shall coincide with the longitudinal centreline of the individual seat.
condition: vehicles equipped with individual seats

text: The H point of the driver test dummy shall coincide within 13 mm in the vertical dimension and 13 mm in the horizontal dimension with a point 6 mm below the position of the H point determined using the procedure of Annex 6, except that the lower leg and thigh segments of the H point machine shall be adjusted to 414 and 401 mm instead of 417 and 432 mm respectively.

The pelvic angle of the driver dummy, measured from the horizontal on the 76.2 mm (3 inch) flat surface of the pelvic angle gauge (GM) drawing 78051-532 inserted into the H point gauging hole, shall be 22.5 degrees plus or minus 2.5 degrees.
The upper legs of the driver test dummy shall rest against the seat cushion to the extent permitted by placement of the feet.
The initial distance between the outboard knee clevis flange surfaces of the driver dummy shall be 270 mm ± 10 mm.

To the extent practicable, the left leg of the driver dummy shall be in vertical longitudinal planes and the right leg in a vertical plane; final adjustment to accommodate placement of feet per paragraph 2.6 is permitted.
The right foot of the driver test dummy shall rest on the undepressed accelerator with the rearmost point of the heel on the floor surface in the plane of the pedal.

If the driver dummy's right foot cannot be placed on the accelerator pedal, it shall be positioned perpendicular to the tibia and placed as far forward as possible in the direction of the centreline of the pedal with the rearmost point of the heel resting on the floor surface.
condition: right foot cannot be placed on the accelerator pedal

text: The heel of the left foot of the driver dummy shall be placed as far forward as possible and rest on the floor pan, the left foot shall be positioned as flat as possible on the toe board, and its longitudinal centreline shall be as parallel as possible to the longitudinal centreline of the vehicle.
For vehicles equipped with a footrest, at the request of the manufacturer the left foot of the driver dummy may be placed on the footrest, its position then being defined by the footrest.
condition: vehicle equipped with a footrest and at manufacturer's request

text: The measuring instruments installed in the driver dummy shall not in any way affect the movement of the dummy during impact.
The temperature of the driver dummy and the system of measuring instruments shall be stabilized before the test and maintained so far as possible within a range between 19 °C and 22.2 °C.

The instrumented HIII fiftieth percentile dummy shall be clothed in formfitting cotton stretch garments with short sleeves and mid-calf length trousers specified in FMVSS 208, drawings 78051-292 and 293 or their equivalent.

A size 11XW shoe meeting the configuration size, sole and heel thickness specifications of MIL S 13192, revision P, with a weight of 0.57 ± 0.1 kg, shall be placed and fastened on each foot of the HIII fiftieth percentile test dummy.

The H 5th point for the Hybrid III fifth percentile female passenger dummy shall be calculated as X5thF = X50thM + (93 mm - 0.323 x XSCL) and Z5thF = Z50thM, where XSCL is the horizontal distance between the H point and the most forward point on the seat cushion.
The transverse instrumentation platform of the head of the HIII fifth percentile passenger dummy shall be horizontal within 2.5°.

To level the head of the HIII fifth percentile passenger dummy in vehicles with upright seats with non-adjustable backs, first the H 5th point shall be adjusted within the limits of paragraph 3.4.3.1, then if still not level the pelvic angle within the limits of paragraph 3.4.3.2, then if still not level the neck bracket the minimum amount necessary to make the head instrumentation platform horizontal within 2.5°.
condition: upright seats with non-adjustable backs

text: To level the head of the HIII fifth percentile passenger dummy in vehicles with adjustable backs, the H 5th point, then the pelvic angle, then the neck bracket shall be adjusted in sequence, and if the head instrumentation platform is still not level, the seat back shall be adjusted to a different angle by the minimum amount necessary to make it horizontal within 2.5°.
condition: seats with adjustable backs

text: The passenger dummy's upper arms shall be in contact with the seat back and the sides of the torso.
The palms of the passenger test dummy shall be in contact with the outside of the thigh and the little finger shall be in contact with the seat cushion.
In vehicles equipped with bench seats, the upper torso of the passenger test dummy shall rest against the seat back.
condition: vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: In vehicles equipped with bench seats, the midsagittal plane of the passenger dummy shall be vertical, parallel to the vehicle's longitudinal centreline and at the same distance from it as the midsagittal plane of the driver dummy.
condition: vehicles equipped with bench seats

text: In vehicles equipped with individual seats, the upper torso of the passenger test dummy shall rest against the seat back.
condition: vehicles equipped with individual seats

text: In vehicles equipped with individual seats, the midsagittal plane of the passenger dummy shall be vertical and shall coincide with the longitudinal centreline of the individual seat.
condition: vehicles equipped with individual seats

text: The H 5th point of the passenger test dummy shall coincide within 13 mm in the horizontal dimension with the H 5th point determined using the procedure of Annex 6 and paragraph 3 of Annex 5.

The pelvic angle of the passenger dummy, measured from the horizontal on the 76.2 mm (3 inch) flat surface of the pelvic angle gauge (GM) drawing 78051-532 inserted into the H point gauging hole, shall be 20 degrees plus or minus 2.5 degrees.
The upper legs of the passenger test dummy shall rest against the seat cushion to the extent permitted by placement of the feet.
The initial distance between the outboard knee clevis flange surfaces of the HIII fifth percentile passenger dummy shall be 229 mm ± 5 mm.
To the extent practicable, both legs of the passenger dummy shall be in vertical longitudinal planes; final adjustment to accommodate placement of feet per paragraph 3.6 is permitted.
The passenger dummy legs shall be positioned as distant as possible from the front end of the seat cushion while the thighs are kept in contact with the seat cushion.

Each passenger dummy leg shall be lowered until the foot contacts the floor while the foot and tibia are kept at a right angle and the thigh inclination angle kept constant; when each heel contacts the floor, the foot shall be rotated so that the toe comes as much in contact as possible with the floor.

If it is not possible to have each passenger dummy foot in contact with the floor, the foot shall be lowered until the calf contacts the front end of the seat cushion or the back of the foot contacts the vehicle interior, and the foot shall be kept as parallel as possible to the floor.
condition: foot cannot contact the floor

text: In case of interference from a vehicle body protrusion, the passenger dummy foot shall be rotated as minimally as possible around the tibia; if interference remains, the femur shall be rotated to resolve or minimize it, and the foot shall be moved inward or outward while the knee separation distance is kept constant.
condition: interference from a vehicle body protrusion

text: The measuring instruments installed in the passenger dummy shall not in any way affect the movement of the dummy during impact.
The temperature of the dummies and the system of measuring instruments shall be stabilized before the test and maintained so far as possible within a range between 19 °C and 22.2 °C.

The instrumented HIII fifth percentile dummy shall be clothed in formfitting cotton stretch garments with short sleeves and mid-calf length trousers specified in FMVSS 208, drawings 78051-292 and 293 or their equivalent.

A size 7.5 W small female shoe meeting the configuration size, sole and heel thickness specifications of MIL-S-21711E, revision P, with a weight of 0.41 ± 0.09 kg, shall be placed and fastened on each foot of the HIII fifth percentile test dummies.
The dummy jacket shall be installed at the position where the bolt hole of the neck lower bracket and the work hole of the dummy jacket are at the same position.

With the dummy at its designated seating position, the belt shall be placed around the dummy and the latch fastened, all slack removed from the lap belt, and the upper torso webbing pulled out of the retractor and allowed to retract, this operation repeated four times.
The shoulder belt shall be positioned so that it is not taken off the shoulder and does not come in contact with the neck of the dummy.
For the Hybrid III fiftieth percentile male dummy, the seat belt path shall be positioned so that the hole of the outer side dummy jacket is not fully hidden by the seat belt.
condition: Hybrid III fiftieth percentile male dummy

text: For the Hybrid III fifth percentile female dummy, the seat belt shall lie between the breasts.
condition: Hybrid III fifth percentile female dummy

text: A 9 to 18 N tension load shall be applied to the lap belt.

If the belt system is equipped with a tension-relieving device, the maximum amount of slack recommended by the manufacturer for normal use in the owner's manual shall be introduced into the upper torso belt.
condition: belt system equipped with a tension-relieving device

text: If the belt system is not equipped with a tension-relieving device, the excess webbing in the shoulder belt shall be retracted by the rewind force of the retractor.
condition: belt system not equipped with a tension-relieving device

text: Where the safety belt and its anchorages are located such that the belt does not lie as required, the safety belt may be manually adjusted and retained by tape.
condition: belt does not lie as required

text: The H point and actual torso angle for seating positions shall be determined according to the procedure described in Addendum 6 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1) (document ECE/TRANS/WP.29/1101/Amend.5).
The trolley shall be so constructed that no permanent deformation appears after the test.
condition: trolley test

text: The trolley shall be so guided that, during the impact phase, the deviation does not exceed 5° in the vertical plane and 2° in the horizontal plane.
condition: trolley test

text: The structure tested on the trolley shall be representative of the series production of the vehicles concerned; components may be replaced or removed only where this clearly has no effect on the test results.
condition: trolley test

text: Adjustments of the structure for the trolley test shall conform to those set out in paragraph 1.4.3 of Annex 3, taking into account paragraph 1.2.1 of Annex 7.
condition: trolley test

text: The structure shall be firmly attached to the trolley in such a way that no relative displacement occurs during the test.
condition: trolley test

text: The method used to fasten the structure to the trolley shall not have the effect of strengthening the seat anchorages or restraint devices, or of producing any abnormal deformation of the structure.
condition: trolley test

text: The angle between the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and the direction of motion of the trolley shall be 0° ± 2°.
condition: trolley test

text: The dummies and their positioning in the trolley test shall conform to the specifications in Annex 3, paragraph 2.
condition: trolley test

text: The transducers measuring the deceleration of the structure during the impact shall be positioned parallel to the longitudinal axis of the trolley according to the specifications of Annex 8 (CFC 180).
condition: trolley test

text: All the measurements on the dummies necessary for checking the listed criteria in the trolley test shall be made as set out in Annex 3, paragraph 5.
condition: trolley test

text: The deceleration curve of the structure during the impact phase shall be such that the variation of speed in relation to time curve obtained by integration at no point differs by more than ±1 m/s from the reference curve of the vehicle concerned as defined in the appendix to Annex 7; a displacement along the time axis of the reference curve may be used to obtain the structure velocity inside the corridor.
condition: trolley test

text: The reference curve ∆V = f(t) shall be obtained by integration of the deceleration curve of the vehicle concerned measured in the frontal collision test against a barrier as provided in paragraph 6 of Annex 3.
condition: trolley test

text: The test may be performed by a method other than deceleration of a trolley only provided that such method complies with the requirement concerning the range of variation of speed described in paragraph 1.6 of Annex 7.
condition: equivalent method used instead of trolley deceleration

text: The absolute value of the linearity error of a data channel at any frequency in the CFC shall be equal to or less than 2.5 per cent of the value of the CAC, over the whole measurement range.
The frequency response of a data channel shall lie within the limiting curves given in Figure 1 of Annex 8, the zero dB line being determined by the calibration factor.
The phase delay time between the input and the output signals of a data channel shall be determined.
The phase delay time of a data channel shall not vary by more than 1/10 FH seconds between 0.03 FH and FH.
A time base shall be recorded and shall at least give 1/100 s with an accuracy of 1 per cent.

The relative time delay between the signal of two or more data channels, regardless of their frequency class, shall not exceed 1 ms excluding delay caused by phase shift; this applies to analogue signals as well as to synchronization pulses and digital signals.
Two or more data channels of which the signals are combined shall have the same frequency class.
condition: if signals of data channels are combined

text: Two or more data channels of which the signals are combined shall not have relative time delay greater than 1/10 FH seconds.
condition: if signals of data channels are combined

text: The transducer cross sensitivity shall be less than 5 per cent in any direction.
A data channel shall be calibrated at least once a year against reference equipment traceable to known standards.
The methods used to carry out a comparison with reference equipment shall not introduce an error greater than 1 per cent of the CAC.
The use of the reference equipment is limited to the frequency range for which it has been calibrated.
Subsystems of a data channel may be evaluated individually provided the results are factored into the accuracy of the total data channel.
condition: if subsystems are evaluated individually

text: The accuracy of the reference equipment for calibration shall be certified or endorsed by an official metrology service.
In static calibration, the errors of the reference equipment for accelerations shall be less than ±1.5 per cent of the channel amplitude class.
In static calibration, the error of the reference equipment for forces shall be less than ±1 per cent of the channel amplitude class.
In static calibration, the error of the reference equipment for displacements shall be less than ±1 per cent of the channel amplitude class.
In dynamic calibration, the error in the reference accelerations expressed as a percentage of the channel amplitude class shall be less than ±1.5 per cent below 400 Hz.
In dynamic calibration, the error in the reference accelerations expressed as a percentage of the channel amplitude class shall be less than ±2 per cent between 400 Hz and 900 Hz.
In dynamic calibration, the error in the reference accelerations expressed as a percentage of the channel amplitude class shall be less than ±2.5 per cent above 900 Hz.
The relative error in the reference time shall be less than 10-5.
The sensitivity coefficient and the linearity error shall be determined by measuring the output signal of the data channel against a known input signal for various values of this signal.
The calibration of the data channel shall cover the whole range of the amplitude class.
For bi-directional data channels, both the positive and negative values shall be used in calibration.
condition: for bi-directional channels

text: If the calibration equipment cannot produce the required input owing to the excessively high values of the quantity to be measured, calibrations shall be carried out within the limits of the calibration standards and these limits shall be recorded in the test report.
condition: if the calibration equipment cannot produce the required input

text: A total data channel shall be calibrated at a frequency or at a spectrum of frequencies having a significant value within the specified range.

The response curves of phase and amplitude against frequency shall be determined by measuring the output signals of the data channel in terms of phase and amplitude against a known input signal, for various values of this signal varying between FL and 10 times the CFC or 3,000 Hz, whichever is lower.
A regular check shall be made to identify any environmental influence (such as electric or magnetic flux, cable velocity, etc.) on the data channels.
If significant output signals due to environmental influence are obtained, corrective action shall be taken, for instance by replacement of cables.
condition: if significant output signals are obtained

text: The CAC of a data channel shall be 1, 2 or 5 to a power of ten.

Transducers should be rigidly secured so that their recordings are affected by vibration as little as possible; any mounting having a lowest resonance frequency equal to at least 5 times the frequency FH of the data channel considered shall be considered valid.

Acceleration transducers should be mounted such that the initial angle of the real measurement axis to the corresponding axis of the reference axis system is not greater than 5°, unless an analytical or experimental assessment of the effect of the mounting on the collected data is made.
When multi-axial accelerations at a point are to be measured, each acceleration transducer axis should pass within 10 mm of that point.
condition: when multi-axial accelerations at a point are measured

text: When multi-axial accelerations at a point are to be measured, the centre of seismic mass of each accelerometer should be within 30 mm of that point.
condition: when multi-axial accelerations at a point are measured

text: Filtering corresponding to the frequencies of the data channel class may be carried out during either recording or processing of data; before recording, analogical filtering at a higher level than CFC should be effected in order to use at least 50 per cent of the dynamic range of the recorder and to reduce the risk of high frequencies saturating the recorder or causing aliasing errors.
The sampling frequency should be equal to at least 8 FH.
The size of digital words should be at least 7 bits and a parity bit.

The results should be presented on A4 size paper (ISO/R 216), and results presented as diagrams should have axes scaled with a measurement unit corresponding to a suitable multiple of the chosen unit (for example, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 millimetres).
SI units shall be used in the presentation of results, except for vehicle velocity, where km/h may be used, and for accelerations due to impact, where g, with g = 9.8 m/s2, may be used.
If a high voltage disconnect function is used, measurements are to be taken from both sides of the device performing the disconnect function.
condition: if a high voltage disconnect function is used

text: Measurements may be taken only between the device performing the disconnect function and the electrical loads only if the high voltage disconnect is integral to the REESS or the energy conversion system and the high-voltage bus of the REESS or the energy conversion system is protected according to protection IPXXB following the impact test.
condition: if the high voltage disconnect is integral to the REESS or energy conversion system and its high-voltage bus is protected to IPXXB after the impact

text: The voltmeter used in the electrical safety test shall measure DC values and have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.
After the impact test, the high voltage bus voltages (Ub, U1, U2) shall be determined, the voltage measurement being made not earlier than 10 seconds, but not later than 60 seconds after the impact.
condition: if voltage is measured and the electric power train is energized during the test

text: For the low electrical energy assessment, prior to the impact a switch S1 and a known discharge resistor Re shall be connected in parallel to the relevant capacitance.
condition: if low electrical energy is assessed by measurement and the electric power train is energized

text: Not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact the switch S1 shall be closed while the voltage Ub and the current Ie are measured and recorded.
condition: if procedure (a) is used and the electric power train is energized

text: The product of the voltage Ub and the current Ie shall be integrated over the period from the moment the switch S1 is closed (tc) until the voltage Ub falls below the high voltage threshold of 60 V DC (th), the resulting integration being the Total Energy (TE) in joules.
condition: if procedure (a) is used and the electric power train is energized

text: When Ub is measured between 10 seconds and 60 seconds after the impact and the capacitance of the X-capacitors (Cx) is specified by the manufacturer, Total Energy shall be calculated as TE = 0.5 x Cx x Ub².
condition: if Cx is specified by the manufacturer and the electric power train is energized

text: When U1 and U2 are measured between 10 seconds and 60 seconds after the impact and the capacitances of the Y-capacitors (Cy1, Cy2) are specified by the manufacturer, Total Energy shall be calculated as TEy1 = 0.5 x Cy1 x U1² and TEy2 = 0.5 x Cy2 x U2².
condition: if Cy1, Cy2 are specified by the manufacturer and the electric power train is energized

text: Following the vehicle impact test any parts surrounding the high voltage components shall be, without the use of tools, opened, disassembled or removed, and all remaining surrounding parts shall be considered part of the physical protection.
The jointed test finger described in Figure 3 shall be inserted into any gaps or openings of the physical protection with a test force of 10 N ± 10 per cent.

If partial or full penetration into the physical protection by the jointed test finger occurs, starting from the straight position both joints of the test finger shall be rotated progressively through an angle of up to 90 degrees with respect to the axis of the adjoining section and placed in every possible position.
condition: if partial or full penetration occurs

text: If appropriate, a low-voltage supply of not less than 40 V and not more than 50 V in series with a suitable lamp should be connected between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts inside the electrical protection barrier or enclosure.
condition: if appropriate

text: The jointed test finger shall be made of metal, except where otherwise specified, with tolerances on dimensions without specific tolerance of +0/-10 seconds on angles, +0/-0.05 mm on linear dimensions up to 25 mm and ±0.2 mm on linear dimensions over 25 mm.
Both joints of the jointed test finger shall permit movement in the same plane and the same direction through an angle of 90° with a 0 to +10° tolerance.

The jointed test finger described in Figure 3 shall be unable to contact high voltage live parts for the requirements of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3 to be met; a mirror or fiberscope may be used to inspect whether the test finger touches the high voltage buses.
If the requirement is verified by a signal circuit between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts, the lamp shall not light.
condition: if verified by a signal circuit

text: When measuring electric resistance with a resistance tester connected to the measuring points (typically electrical chassis and electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier), the resistance tester shall have a measurement current of at least 0.2 A and a resolution of 0.01 Ω or less.
condition: if test method (a) using a resistance tester is used

text: Using the resistance tester method, the resistance R between the electrical chassis and the electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier shall be less than 0.1 Ω.
condition: if test method (a) using a resistance tester is used

text: Using the DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter method, the voltage of the DC power supply shall be adjusted so that the current flow becomes at least 0.2 A, the current I and voltage U measured and the resistance calculated as R = U / I.
condition: if test method (b) using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter is used

text: Using the DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter method, the resistance R shall be less than 0.1 Ω.
condition: if test method (b) using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter is used

text: If lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement, each lead wire shall be independently connected to the electrical protection barrier/enclosure/electrical chassis.
condition: if lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement

text: The isolation resistance for each high voltage bus of the vehicle shall be measured or determined by calculating the measurement values of each part or component unit of the high voltage bus.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: All measurements for calculating voltage(s) and electrical isolation are made after a minimum of 10 seconds after the impact.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: The isolation resistance measurement is conducted by selecting an appropriate measurement method from those listed in paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.2. of Annex 9, depending on the electrical charge of the live parts or the isolation resistance, with the range of the electrical circuit to be measured clarified in advance using electrical circuit diagrams.
condition: vehicles equipped with electric power train

text: If the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other, isolation resistance shall be measured for each electrical circuit.
condition: if the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other

text: Modifications necessary for measuring the isolation resistance (such as removal of the cover to reach the live parts, drawing of measurement lines and change in software) may be carried out, provided they do not influence the test results.

Where measured values are not stable due to the operation of the on-board isolation resistance monitoring system, the device may be stopped or removed; when the device is removed, a set of drawings shall be used to prove that the isolation resistance between the live parts and the electrical chassis remains unchanged.
condition: if measured values are not stable due to the on-board isolation resistance monitoring system

text: Utmost care shall be exercised to avoid short circuit and electric shock during isolation resistance measurement since it might require direct operations of the high-voltage circuit.

For the measurement method using DC voltage from external sources, an isolation resistance test instrument capable of applying a DC voltage higher than the working voltage of the high voltage bus shall be used.
condition: measurement using DC voltage from external sources

text: The isolation resistance test instrument is connected between the live parts and the electrical chassis and the isolation resistance is measured by applying a DC voltage at least half of the working voltage of the high voltage bus.
condition: measurement using DC voltage from external sources

text: If the system has several voltage ranges in a conductively connected circuit and some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit, the isolation resistance between those components and the electrical chassis can be measured separately by applying at least half of their own working voltage with those components disconnected.
condition: if the system has several voltage ranges and some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit

text: When using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source, the high voltage bus is energized by the vehicle's own REESS and/or energy conversion system and the voltage level of the REESS and/or energy conversion system throughout the test shall be at least the nominal operating voltage as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: measurement using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The voltmeter used in the isolation resistance test shall measure DC values and have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.
condition: measurement using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The high voltage bus voltage (Ub) is measured and recorded as shown in Figure 1; Ub shall be equal to or greater than the nominal operating voltage of the REESS and/or energy conversion system as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: measurement using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The voltage (U1) between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis is measured and recorded.
condition: measurement using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The voltage (U2) between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis is measured and recorded.
condition: measurement using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: If U1 is greater than or equal to U2, a standard known resistance (Ro) is inserted between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, the voltage U1' is measured, and the electrical isolation is calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U1' - 1/U1).
condition: if U1 is greater than or equal to U2

text: If U2 is greater than U1, a standard known resistance (Ro) is inserted between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, the voltage U2' is measured, and the electrical isolation is calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U2' - 1/U2).
condition: if U2 is greater than U1

text: The isolation resistance (in Ω/V) is obtained by dividing the electrical isolation value Ri (in Ω) by the working voltage of the high voltage bus (in V).
condition: measurement using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: An appropriate coating may be applied, if necessary, to the physical protection (casing) to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the test.
Unless the manufacturer provides means to differentiate between the leakage of different liquids, all liquid leakage shall be considered as the electrolyte.
condition: unless the manufacturer provides means to differentiate between leakage of different liquids

text: Compliance with REESS retention requirements shall be determined by visual inspection.

Prior to conducting the crash test, instrumentation is installed in the hydrogen storage system to perform the required pressure and temperature measurements if the standard vehicle does not already possess instrumentation with the required accuracy.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle without instrumentation of the required accuracy

text: The hydrogen storage system is purged, if necessary, following manufacturer directions to remove impurities from the container before filling with compressed hydrogen or helium gas.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The target fill pressure shall be determined from the equation Ptarget = NWP x (273 + To) / 288, where NWP is the nominal working pressure (MPa) and To is the ambient temperature to which the storage system is expected to settle.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The container is filled to a minimum of 95 per cent of the targeted fill pressure and allowed to settle (stabilize) prior to conducting the crash test.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The main stop valve and shut-off valves for hydrogen gas, located in the downstream hydrogen gas piping, are in the normal driving condition kept open immediately prior to the impact.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Sensors are selected to measure either the build-up of the hydrogen or helium gas or the reduction in oxygen due to displacement of air by leaking hydrogen/helium.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Sensors are calibrated to traceable references to ensure an accuracy of ±5 per cent at the targeted criteria of 4 per cent hydrogen or 3 per cent helium by volume in air, and a full scale measurement capability of at least 25 per cent above the target criteria.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The gas concentration sensor shall be capable of a 90 per cent response to a full scale change in concentration within 10 seconds.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Prior to the crash impact, a sensor is located at a distance within 250 mm of the headliner above the driver's seat or near the top centre of the passenger compartment.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Prior to the crash impact, a sensor is located at a distance within 250 mm of the floor in front of the rear (or rear most) seat in the passenger compartment.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: Prior to the crash impact, a sensor is located at a distance within 100 mm of the top of luggage compartments inside the vehicle that are not directly affected by the particular crash impact to be conducted.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The sensors are securely mounted on the vehicle structure or seats and protected for the planned crash test from debris, air bag exhaust gas and projectiles; measurements following the crash are recorded by instruments located in the vehicle or by remote transmission.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: The test may be conducted outdoors in an area protected from the wind and possible solar effects, or indoors in a space large enough or ventilated to prevent the build-up of hydrogen to more than 10 per cent of the targeted criteria in the passenger and luggage compartments.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: For a storage system filled with hydrogen, the hydrogen gas pressure P0 (MPa) and temperature T0 (°C) are measured immediately before the impact and then at a time interval Δt (min) after the impact.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The time interval Δt for the hydrogen leak test starts when the vehicle comes to rest after the impact and continues for at least 60 minutes.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The time interval Δt shall be increased if necessary to accommodate measurement accuracy for a storage system with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa, calculated as Δt = VCHSS x NWP /1,000 x ((-0.027 x NWP +4) x Rs – 0.21) -1.7 x Rs, where Rs = Ps / NWP.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa

text: If the calculated value of Δt for the hydrogen leak test is less than 60 minutes, Δt is set to 60 minutes.
condition: if calculated Δt is less than 60 minutes

text: The initial mass of hydrogen in the storage system is calculated as Po' = Po x 288 / (273 + T0); ρo' = –0.0027 x (P0')2 + 0.75 x P0' + 1.07; Mo = ρo' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The final mass of hydrogen in the storage system at the end of Δt is calculated as Pf' = Pf x 288 / (273 + Tf); ρf' = –0.0027 x (Pf')2 + 0.75 x Pf' + 1.07; Mf = ρf' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: The average hydrogen flow rate over the time interval is calculated as VH2 = (Mf-Mo) / Δt x 22.41 / 2.016 x (Ptarget /Po) in NL/min.
condition: storage system filled with compressed hydrogen

text: For a storage system filled with helium, the helium gas pressure P0 (MPa) and temperature T0 (°C) are measured immediately before the impact and then at a predetermined time interval after the impact.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The time interval Δt for the helium leak test starts when the vehicle comes to rest after the impact and continues for at least 60 minutes.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The time interval Δt shall be increased if necessary to accommodate measurement accuracy for a storage system with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa, calculated as Δt = VCHSS x NWP /1000 x ((-0.028 x NWP +5.5) x Rs – 0.3) – 2.6 x Rs, where Rs = Ps / NWP.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium with a large volume operating up to 70 MPa

text: If the value of Δt for the helium leak test is less than 60 minutes, Δt is set to 60 minutes.
condition: if Δt is less than 60 minutes

text: The initial mass of helium in the storage system is calculated as Po' = Po x 288 / (273 + T0); ρo' = –0.0043 x (P0')2 + 1.53 x P0' + 1.49; Mo = ρo' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The final mass of helium in the storage system at the end of Δt is calculated as Pf' = Pf x 288 / (273 + Tf); ρf' = –0.0043 x (Pf')2 + 1.53 x Pf' + 1.49; Mf = ρf' x VCHSS.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The average helium flow rate over the time interval is calculated as VHe = (Mf-Mo) / Δt x 22.41 / 4.003 x (Ptarget/ Po) in NL/min.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: The average volumetric flow of helium is converted to the average hydrogen flow by VH2 = VHe / 0.75.
condition: storage system filled with compressed helium

text: Post-crash data collection in enclosed spaces commences when the vehicle comes to rest; data from the sensors are collected at least every five seconds and continue for a period of 60 minutes after the test.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: A first-order lag (time constant) up to a maximum of five seconds may be applied to the concentration measurements to provide smoothing and filter the effects of spurious data points.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle

text: In the case of a compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle, compliance with paragraphs 5.2.7.1. to 5.2.7.3. shall be shown.
condition: compressed hydrogen-fuelled vehicle
